assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin action, proglucagon processing, GLP-1 peptide characterization) led to therapies that have transformed type 2 diabetes and obesity care. Mechanistic discovery and very large clinical impact are both clear and unusually durable.
assessment.attribution: Drucker and Holst established the physiology and therapeutic rationale; Mojsov's early peptide chemistry and identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) form is a contested but substantial contribution. Knudsen's work is mainly drug development and is more naturally recognized separately. The list omits some other discoverers of the field, and I cannot verify the full priority record from memory.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and approved drugs with large outcome trials; recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among physiologists, peptide chemists and drug developers is disputed and limited to three.
Whether the committee would prefer a discovery-only configuration over one including industrial development is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells directed by chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new therapeutic modality, with both conceptual originality and clear patient benefit.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain contributed early CAR design with costimulation and preclinical proof; June led the pivotal clinical translation; Rosenberg's work on adoptive T-cell therapy and early CD19 CAR clinical studies is foundational to the field. Eshhar and others who contributed first-generation CAR concepts are not in the supplied credit list, which limits a fully fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and years of follow-up confirm efficacy in hematologic cancers; durability, toxicity and solid-tumor limits remain active issues, but the core discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Missing early CAR originators in the credited names complicates fair allocation.
Solid-tumor efficacy and long-term safety are not yet resolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new form of organelle-to-nucleus signaling (IRE1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing, ATF6, PERK) and underlies protein quality control, secretory physiology and disease mechanisms. The discovery is original, clear and conceptually broad.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori independently and complementarily elucidated the pathway: Mori identified the UPR transcriptional elements and ATF6, and Walter identified IRE1 signaling and unconventional mRNA splicing. This is a clean two-person configuration; I cannot independently verify every contributing lab's priority.
assessment.maturity: Over three decades of independent confirmation across yeast and mammals, with extensive follow-on work; recognition is mature, with translational implications still developing.
uncertainties: Other contributors to IRE1 and PERK discoveries are not credited in this list.
Direct clinical translation is still emerging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology a genetically targeted, millisecond-scale way to control cell activity, enabling causal circuit studies across many fields. Methodological originality and impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: Credit spans channelrhodopsin discovery and characterization (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg), first neuronal applications (Boyden, Deisseroth, Miesenböck) and tool development. A three-person set is a hard compromise; I chose the discovery of the channel plus the leading neuronal application, but this leaves out Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck and is genuinely contested.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted for over fifteen years with extensive independent replication; clinical applications are limited so far, which may affect the prize category fit.
uncertainties: Six credited names cannot be reduced to three without leaving out a decisive contributor.
Therapeutic and physiological-medicine impact is still early compared with the research-tool impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR signaling is a central regulator of cell growth, metabolism and ageing, linked to cancer, immunology and metabolic disease, and the pathway has clinical drugs (rapamycin analogs).
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR genetically in yeast and its function in growth control; Schreiber's chemical-biology work on FKBP12-rapamycin contributed to the target identification. Sabatini and others made major mammalian-pathway contributions, and Sabatini's inclusion is also complicated by personal circumstances I cannot assess from here. Hall is the clearest core laureate; the second slot is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed and foundational, with a large literature; recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Allocation among Hall, Schreiber, Sabatini and earlier rapamycin work (Sehgal, Heitman et al.) is unresolved.
Pathway complexity means the prize might need a narrower, better-defined citation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and BCR-ABL inhibition established the paradigm of targeted kinase-inhibitor therapy and turned chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal into a manageable disease. The impact is large and the discovery is clear.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (chemistry and inhibitor discovery), Druker (clinical proof and trials) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and next-generation inhibitors) form a plausible translational configuration. The underlying BCR-ABL oncogene discoveries by others are outside the credited set.
assessment.maturity: Approved for over two decades with durable survival data; very mature and already recognized by major prizes.
uncertainties: Translational and drug-development work may be seen as less aligned with the prize's emphasis on discovery.
Not credited are the earlier BCR-ABL fusion discoverers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense modulation of SMN2 splicing (nusinersen) is a clear mechanistic discovery that produced the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy and validated splicing-modifying oligonucleotides as a drug class.
assessment.attribution: Krainer's work on splicing regulation and SMN2 exon 7 inclusion and Bennett's antisense chemistry and drug platform are complementary and form a coherent pair; other contributors, such as Hua and Singh in the Krainer program, are not credited in the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with several years of clinical follow-up and subsequent related therapies; fairly mature but the field is still young compared with the oldest candidates.
uncertainties: Long-term durability and the relative role of platform chemistry versus the splicing insight are uncertain.
The credit may be seen as divided between an academic discovery and an industrial platform.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 as a survival rather than proliferation oncogene redefined cell death control in cancer and led directly to BH3-mimetic therapy (venetoclax), connecting basic discovery to a new targeted cancer treatment.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams drove the characterization of BCL-2 and the family; Vaux demonstrated the cell-survival function of BCL-2 in vivo and in cooperation with Myc. Tsujimoto, Korsmeyer and others also have notable claims, and Strasser is credited here but ranks behind the three chosen. I am uncertain about the exact priority record.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by decades of independent work and approved clinical drugs; mature and timely.
uncertainties: Priority among Tsujimoto, Korsmeyer, Cory, Adams and Vaux is not fully captured by the supplied credit list.
Part of the cell-death field was already recognized by the 2002 prize, which may reduce the novelty of the claim.
